title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs): Treasury Repurchase Agreement Risk Management

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York - Treasury Market Practices Group

summary: The Treasury Market Practices Group (TMPG) issued best practice recommendations for U.S. Treasury repo risk management on May 22, 2025, emphasizing the application of haircuts or margin on repo transactions to mitigate counterparty credit risk, liquidity risk, and market risk. The guidance addresses systemic risks in the non-centrally cleared bilateral repo market where risk management practices lack consistency and transparency. TMPG recommends implementation by June 2026 using a risk-based, rolling approach.
key_points: TMPG recommends that all Treasury repos be prudently risk managed with haircuts or margin applied alongside other techniques such as position limits, netting agreements, and portfolio margining
The non-centrally cleared bilateral repo market lacks consistency and transparency in risk management practices, potentially leaving leverage improperly understood and priced

A working group formed in February 2023 developed the recommendations, including representatives from dealers, money funds, hedge funds, asset managers, and staff from Treasury and the Federal Reserve Bank of New York
Not all repo transactions will be eligible for central clearing once mandatory central clearing is in full effect, meaning a segment of the NCCBR market will remain outside central clearing
Centrally cleared repos already adhere to the best practice as they are managed through robust margining and risk management regimes consistent with the recommendations
Implementation deadline is June 2026, with firms advised to prioritize their most material counterparty exposures on a rolling basis
why_it_matters: The Treasury repo market is critical market infrastructure; inadequate risk management poses systemic risks that could impair market functioning during stress periods. Market participants, clearing banks, and money market funds should ensure their legal agreements, policies, and procedures align with these best practices by the June 2026 deadline. This guidance is especially relevant as the SEC's mandatory central clearing expansion continues.
market_structure_context: The document provides detailed guidance on Treasury repo market plumbing, specifically addressing risk management in the non-centrally cleared bilateral repo market. It defines expectations for legally enforceable documentation including margining regimes, valuation of exposures, and close-out netting. The guidance distinguishes between centrally cleared and bilateral repo risk management frameworks and notes that implementation should be prioritized by counterparty exposure materiality.
